title: Hemorrhagic Longitudinally Extensive Transverse Myelitis (LETM) as a First Presentation of Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD): A Case Report and Literature Review
case_prompt:
A 51-year-old man presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of lower limb paralysis. He also reported vertigo, nausea, vomiting, and a severe frontotemporal headache. He had no chronic medical conditions, took no regular medications, and denied substance use, smoking, alcohol use, trauma, fever, or recent vaccination. There was no family history of autoimmune or neurological disease. On examination he was alert and oriented; vital signs were within normal limits. Nonneurologic findings were unremarkable. Muscle strength was 4/5 in both upper extremities and 1/5 in both lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes were brisk in all limbs, and bilateral Babinski signs were present.  
  
Initial brain and spinal MRI at the referring hospital demonstrated longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions, and he was treated with high-dose methylprednisolone and five sessions of plasmapheresis, with partial improvement. Shortly thereafter he developed COVID-19 infection with worsening of symptoms and received intravenous immunoglobulin without significant recovery. He was then referred to our hospital. Review of prior imaging revealed a longitudinally extensive T2-hyperintense spinal cord lesion with T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhage.  
   
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis, including herpes simplex virus-1, herpes simplex virus-2, varicella zoster virus, and Epstein–Barr virus studies, was normal. Routine laboratory investigations were within normal limits. Tests for venereal disease, vitamin B12 level, HIV, antinuclear antibodies, coagulation studies, and paraneoplastic panels were normal. Spinal cord angiography showed no abnormalities. Serum myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Infectious myelitis — “Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis including herpes simplex virus‐1 (HSV‐1), herpes simplex virus‐2 (HSV‐2), Varicella zoster virus (VZV), and Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) was normal.”
2. Vascular malformation (spinal arteriovenous malformation) — “Spinal cord angiography did not show any abnormality.”
3. Coagulopathy or systemic/paraneoplastic disease — “Venereal disease research laboratory test, vitamin B12 serum level, Human immunodeficiency viruses (HIV), anti‐nuclear antibody (ANA), anti‐coagulopathy, and para neoplastic investigations were normal…”
4. MOG antibody–associated disease — “Serum myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibodies were negative…”
5. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder — “he had positive AQP4‐IgG.”
